what: In the middle of a black curtain, three 3:2 bordered boxes show 000 slowly filling toward 96 by 2.5% of the remaining distance (minimum .08) every 0.1 seconds. When ready, 98 → 100 shows clearly for two frames and holds for .18s. Then the numbers drop 8px and fade out, the curtain folds to the size and corners of the Hero window (the element picked by to) over .9s cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1), then disappears after .42s and fires fx:done.

options.ready: Ready time (s), default 2.6 — meanwhile the number slowly rises toward 96
options.wait: If true, ready is not used and it finishes when the consumer sends fx:go to the element (when images·models have all arrived)
options.to: CSS selector of the element the curtain folds into (e.g. .hero-window) — if none, it folds into a single point at the center
options.hold: Time to stay after showing 100 (seconds), default .18
options.fade: Duration for the folded curtain to vanish (s), default .42
options.fx:collapse: Event the element fires when it starts to fold — the original turns the logo color to the page color here

use: 000
note: The number is not the real download amount but a tempo — the original counts up on its own to 96 so heavy loading does not look frozen, and shows 100 only once everything has loaded. The number of cells equals the number of digit children

from.where: shared.js runLoader · .px-loader — three 000→100 cells, and once full they fold into the Hero window (.px-portal, min(520px,56vw), 1.55:1, 30px corners)
